title: Italy Fines Meta Over User Photo Access
summary: Italy has fined Meta hundreds of millions of dollars over access to Android users' photos and videos.
paragraphs: According to DW and Al Jazeera, Italian regulators have slapped Meta with an €805mn (or $880m) fine over access to photos and multimedia content from Italian users via the Facebook application for Android devices. CNBC reported the fine as $887 million for allegedly accessing Android users' photographs and videos without obtaining consent or informing them.

The BBC reported that the social media giant is accused of failing to inform about 20 million users that it had access to their photos. Al Jazeera added that the regulator cited Meta's lack of cooperation and the large number of people affected as factors contributing to the size of the fine, while Meta has not yet commented on the allegations according to DW.

title: US Flights Resume After Nationwide Ground Stop Caused by Data Overload
summary: U.S. flights are gradually resuming following a rare and lengthy nationwide ground stop caused by overloaded routers.
paragraphs: According to France 24 and the BBC, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday after routers became overloaded with data. More than 8,200 flights, representing over 31% of scheduled departures in the United States, were canceled during the disruption, which lasted nearly five hours and marked the longest such stoppage since September 11, 2001.
